 How to choose this product
A Rockwell hardness tester measures the hardness of a material by means of an indentation trial. The indenter is pressed against the surface of the sample with a specific amount of force, the minor load. The depth of the impression serves as a zero point. Additional force is applied, the major load. The force is reduced until the indicator needle comes to a stop at zero. The depth difference indicates hardness.
 Applications
This type of test can be used to determine the hardness of both soft and hard materials. Different indenters are employed with materials of varying hardness.
 Technologies
Rockwell devices use different scales, depending on the hardness of the test piece. In addition, there are both traditional and superficial versions of the test. While the same indenters are used for both, the superficial test is used on thinner or more delicate materials.
 Advantages
- Direct display of the measured value
- Rapid sample preparation and measurement
- Automatic models available
- Not affected by irregular surfaces
 Disadvantages
- The test piece must have a certain minimum thickness
